calls.head: Watch the Islanders’ puck management
calls.body: The Rangers turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Islanders are one of the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Islanders.
calls.call: The Rangers get at least their usual 7.5% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: NY Rangers 10th for chances off turnovers (7.5% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · NY Islanders 31st for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: 18.3% of NY Rangers’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.5%.

calls.head: The Rangers’ power play has a target
calls.body: The Islanders’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Rangers’ power play is near the top of the league. Discipline matters more than usual for the Islanders tonight.
calls.call: The Rangers’ power play creates at least their usual 7.7 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: NY Rangers 10th for power play (7.7 expected goals per 60) · NY Islanders 30th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: NY Rangers’s power play created 25.7 expected goals per 60 in 3:52 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 7.7, and scored 1 goal.
calls.beyond: NY Rangers’s power play created 25.7 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.7 and a league average of 7.5. A team strays this far about once every 800 games.

calls.head: Bodies will fly
calls.body: The Islanders and the Rangers are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
calls.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 112.
calls.nums: Hit score (100 is league average): NY Islanders 107 (9th), NY Rangers 118 (2nd)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 4 games this season
calls.happened: The two teams’ combined hit score was 108, against their usual 112 (100 is league average, after adjusting for the arena’s scorer).

NYI.head: We had this close to even (41% for NY Islanders), and it went NY Rangers’s way.

surprises.head: NY Rangers tried a different line
surprises.body: C. Beaudoin, J. Chmelar, O. Bjorkstrand played 6:14 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of NY Rangers’s usual lines.

story.head: A hat trick for Lafrenière
paras: Oliver Bjorkstrand scored twice, opening the scoring midway through the first. Alexis Lafrenière scored three.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Rangers win about seven in ten.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Rangers.
Oliver Bjorkstrand scored his first goal of the season.
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
